questions.question: The average height of a group of 12 students is 170 cm. Four students of heights 154 cm, 157 cm, 165 cm and 172 cm left the group. What is the new average height (in cm) of the group?
questions.solution:
Given: 

The average height of a group of 12 students is 170 cm. Four students of heights 154 cm, 157 cm, 165 cm and 172 cm left the group.

Concept used:

Total = Average × Number of entities

Calculation:

Let the new average of the group be Q.

According to the question,

(12 - 4) × Q + 154 + 157 + 165 + 172 = 170 × 12

⇒ Q = 174

**∴ The new average height of the group is 174 cm. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

The average height of 12 students is 170 cm.

Sum of heights of 12 students = 170 × 12 = 2040 cm

Four students of heights 154 cm, 157 cm, 165 cm and 172 cm left the group.

Sum of heights of remaining students = 2040 - 154 - 157 - 165 - 172 = 1392 cm

New average = 1392/8 = 174 cm

questions.question: The cost price of an article is 25% less than its selling price. What is the profit or loss percentage?
questions.solution:
Given:

The cost price of an article is 25% less than its selling price

Concept used:

Profit Percentage = {{Selling Price - Cost Price} over Cost Price} times 100\% 

Calculation:

Let the selling price be Rs. 100.

Hence. the cost price must be = 100 - 100 × 25% = Rs. 75

thus, profit% = {(100 - 75) over 75} times 100\% approx 33.33\% 

**∴ The profit percentage is 33.33%.**

In 2015, there was an increase of 50% and 25% of expenditure on Cricket and Other Sports, respectively, compared to the previous year. What was the ratio of the expenditure on Cricket to that on Other Sports in 2014?
questions.solution:
Calculation:

In 2014,

Share of Other Sports = 59 ÷ (1 + {25 over 100}) = 47.2° 

Share of Cricket = 85 ÷ (1 + {50 over 100}) ≈ 56.67°

Hence, ratio = 56.67 : 47.2 = 425 : 354

**∴ 425 : 354 was the ratio of the expenditure on Cricket to that on Other Sports in 2014.**

questions.question: A and B travel the same distance at speeds of 8 km/h and 12 km/h, respectively. If B takes 30 minutes less than that taken by A, what is the distance (in km) travelled by each one of them?
questions.solution:
Given: 

Speed of A = 8 kmph

Speed of B = 12 kmph

B takes 30 minutes i.e. {1 over 2} hour less than that taken by A

Concept used:

Time × Speed = Distance

Calculation:

Let the time taken by A be Q hours.

According to the question,

8 × Q = 12 × (Q - 1/2)

⇒ Q = 1.5

Hence, distance travelled = 8 × 1.5 = 12 km

**∴ The distance travelled by each one of them is 12 km.**

questions.question: A and B can do a piece of work in 15 days, while B and C can do the same work in 12 days, and C and A in 10 days. They all work together for 5 days, and then B and C leave. How many days more will A take to finish the work?
questions.solution:
Given:

A and B can do a piece of work in 15 days, while B and C can do the same work in 12 days, and C and A in 10 days.

They all work together for 5 days, and then B and C leave.

Concept used:

Total Work = Work done each day × Total time taken (in days)

Calculation:

LCM (15, 12, 10) = 60

Let the total work be the LCM of the time taken by them.

Hence, total work = 60 units

Thus,

A & B together do each day = 60 ÷ 15 = 4 units

B & C together do each day = 60 ÷ 12 = 5 units

C & A together do each day = 60 ÷ 10 = 6 units

Hence,

A + B = 4 ....(1)

B + C = 5 ....(2)

C + A = 6 ....(3)

Now, 2(A + B + C) = 15 ....(4)

Solving these equations we get,

A = 2.5; B = 1.5; C = 3.5.

Now, in 5 days work done = 5 × (A + B + C) = 5 × 7.5 = 37.5 units

Remaining work = 60 - 37.5 = 22.5 work

Time taken by A to complete the work = 22.5 ÷ 2.5 = 9 days

**∴ Time taken by A to complete the work is 9 days.**

questions.question: Two numbers are 32% and 48% more than a third number. What percentage (correct to two decimal places) is the second number of the first?
questions.solution:
Given:

Two numbers are 32% and 48% more than a third number.

**Concept Used:**

Incremented value = Initial value × (1 + increment%)

Calculation:

Let the third number be Q.

Hence,

the first number = Q × 1.32 = 1.32Q

the second number = Q × 1.48 = 1.48Q

Required % = {1.48Q over 1.32Q} × 100\% ≈ 112.12%

**∴ 112.12% is the second number of the first.**

questions.question: P sold a mobile phone to Q at 25% profit. However, Q sold it to R at a loss of 10%. If R paid Rs. 3,240 for the mobile phone, what was the price (in Rs.) paid by P for it?
questions.solution:
Given:

P sold a mobile phone to Q at 25% profit. 

Q sold it to R at a loss of 10%

R paid Rs. 3,240 for the mobile phone

Concept used:

Selling Price = Cost Price × (1 + Profit%)

Resultant percentage change for two successive percentage increment of A% and B% = {A + B + (AB/100)}%

Calculation:

Profit incurred in the entire transaction = 25 + (-10) + {25 × (-10)} over 100 = 12.5%

Hence, the price paid by P for it = 3240 ÷ (1 + 12.5/100) = Rs. 2880

**∴ Rs. 2880 was paid by P for the mobile phone.**

questions.question: The total number of students in three classes of an Engineering Institute is 885. The strength of the students in the first two classes are in the ratio of 4 ∶ 9. The ratio of the number of students in the second and the third classes is 6 ∶ 11. How many students are there in the class that has the maximum number of students?
questions.solution:
Given:

In the Engineering Institute, ratios of the strength of the students in the classes,

First : Second = 4 : 9

Second : Third = 6 : 11

Total students = 885

Concept used:

Ratio Proportion

Calculation:

According to the question,

First : Second = 4 : 9 = 8 : 18

Second : Third = 6 : 11 = 18 : 33

Hence, First : Second : Third = 8 : 18 : 33

Thus, the number of students in the class that has the maximum number of students = {33 over (8 + 18 + 33)} times 885 = 495

**∴ The number of students in the class that has the maximum number of students is 495.**

questions.question: In how many years will the interest on a certain sum of money at 5% p.a. be three-eights of itself? (Express your answer in years and months)
questions.solution:
Given:

Rate of interest = 5%

Interest incurred = three-eights of the principal

Concept used:

Simple Interest, SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

where

P = Principal amount

R = Rate of interest per year

T = Time in years

Calculation:

Let the principal amount be Rs. P and time required be T years.

According to the question,

{P times 5 times T} over 100 = {3 over 8} times P 

⇒ T = 7.5 

Hence, time required = 7.5 years = 7 years 6 months

**∴ In 7 years 6 months the interest on a certain sum of money at 5% p.a. will be three-eights of itself.**

questions.question: The LCM of (18)/(5), (6)/(5) and (18)/(125) is:

(18)/(5), (6)/(5) and (18)/(125)

LCM of fractions = { LCM (Numerators) over HCF (Denominators)}

Calculation:

 LCM ((18)/(5), (6)/(5),(18)/(125)) = { LCM (18, 6, 18) over HCF (5, 5, 125)} = {18 over 5} = 3.6

**∴ The LCM of (18)/(5), (6)/(5) and (18)/(125) is 3.6.**

questions.question: The average of 75 scores is 45. The average of the first 50 scores is 42 and that of the last 26 scores is 52. What is the 50th score?
questions.solution:
Given:

The average of 75 scores is 45.

The average of the first 50 scores is 42 and that of the last 26 scores is 52.

Concept used:

Total = Average × Number of entities

Calculation:

According to the question,

1st + 2ⁿd + 3rd + ... + 50th = 50 × 42 = 2100 ....(1)

75th + 74th + 73rd + ... + 50th = 26 × 52 = 1352 ....(2)

1st + 2nd + 3rd + ... + 50th + ... + 73rd + 74th + 75th = 75 × 45 = 3375 ....(3)

Now, (1) + (2) - (3), we get,

50th = 2100 + 1352 - 3375 = 77

**∴ The 50th score is 77.**

questions.question: The present value of an old car is Rs. 5,40,000. Its value depreciates at 25% per annum. What was its value (in Rs.) 2 years ago?
questions.solution:
Given:

Present value = Rs. 5,40,000.

Its value depreciates at 25% per annum

Concept used:

Depreciated value = P(1 - R/100)n

where

P = Principal amount

R = Rate of depreciation

N = Time in years

Calculation:

Let its value 2 years ago be Q.

According to the question,

Q (1 - 25/100)² = 540000

⇒ Q = 960000

**∴ its value 2 years ago was Rs. 9,60,000.**
